Local PLS financing, settlement and bounded pDAI support
29 September 2026. Accounting companion to the conditional PulseChain report. This is an illustrative
model, not a measurement of current markets, a record of execution, or an administrative action plan.
The holder's contemplated exit is selling pDAI for PLS on PulseChain. Neither Ethereum redemption
nor a bridge-out transaction is required for that exit.
Resolutions supplied by this study
Review point Resolution
1 — Meaning of backing Distinguish custody coverage, source solvency, redemption
timing, funded local exchange and the holder's local PLS
exit. None is silently substituted for another.
2 — Origin of financing Complete illustrative borrowing, issuer and relayer ledgers
identify the participant whose existing local assets fund the
purchase, plus the asset or claim received in exchange.
6 — Portal and ordinary debt A fully settled Portal example requires a specific top-up and
retains receipt liabilities; ordinary debt repayment is
reconciled separately. Neither payment automatically
performs the other.
8 — Intermediate cash A per-asset, per-step inequality requires cash or committed
drawable credit before each payment, even when terminal
net assets are positive.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 289

Review point Resolution
9 — Shared capital Budgets are exclusive allocations of spendable inventory.
Shared collateral, LP reserves and relayer cash are
consolidated once.
10 — Assets returning to markets A holder exit, aT oken redemption, collateral withdrawal and
bridge-receipt return are distinct modeled flows. Local pDAI
exits require none of the latter operations.
11 — Bounded support A fee-inclusive recurrence supports specified local PLS
execution for a finite seller sequence and defined reference
trajectory, conditional on an explicit reserve budget.
These resolve the conceptual/accounting objections within stated models. They do not turn illustrative
funding or configurable interfaces into historical facts about the named wallets.
The relevant assets and claims
Let R be a transferable source investment receipt and X its exclusive PulseChain representation. The
source investment remains invested when R changes custodian. Holding X is not a second independent
ownership of R in addition to an unrestricted source claim held by the depositor.
A source receipt's unit coverage concerns whether its claimed assets or shares exist. Solvency concerns
the realizable assets relative to obligations. Liquidity concerns when payments can occur. Local
purchasing capacity concerns whether an exact accepted asset receives actual pDAI, PLS or an
intermediate token from a funded counterparty. The pDAI holder's exit is a separate local swap.
For a finite transaction, technical acceptance and funded output can suffice even if the incoming claim
has weak economic recovery. The accepting market, lender or issuer then retains that exposure. This
may change future quotes or create losses, but it is not a reason to declare the initial local purchase
mechanically impossible. Conversely, accurate custody alone does not supply the market's PLS output.
The ledgers below use illustrative token counts. No unit of R, X or a newly issued token is assumed
to equal one dollar. Figures such as 700 PLS are stipulated exchange amounts, not observed prices.
Transaction and operating costs are zero in these small ledgers or paid from separately allocated funds;
the quantitative price model below explicitly includes AMM trading fees.
Funded borrowing: the investor retains a pledged claim and a debt
Assume source custody already holds 100 R and 100 exclusive X are held by the investor. The lender
accepts X as collateral and has 1,000 PLS of spendable local inventory. It lends 700 PLS against the 100
X. Let d(700) denote the actual pDAI output from spending that 700 PLS through a specified local market.
Participant Before After collateral placement, loan
and purchase
Source investment Assets underlying 100 R remain
invested
Unchanged investment, ignoring yield/
loss
Source bridge custodian 100 R allocated to outstanding X Same 100 R allocation
Investor/borrower 100 unpledged X; no loan or PLS
proceeds
d(700) pDAI; beneficial interest in 100
pledged X; owes 700 PLS principal
plus agreed accrual
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 290

Participant Before After collateral placement, loan
and purchase
Lender 1,000 PLS; no loan receivable 300 PLS; 700 PLS loan receivable;
holds/enforces pledge of 100 X
pDAI/PLS market Its initial inventory Receives 700 PLS and pays d(700)
pDAI
The lender's loan receivable and pledged X are not two independent 700-PLS assets. The pledge secures
collection of that same debt. The borrower cannot simultaneously treat pledged X as available
unencumbered collateral elsewhere unless an explicitly permitted subordinate structure is separately
accounted.
This ledger establishes a financed purchase during the loan term. It is not necessary to repay the future
principal before spending the borrowed proceeds. For an illustrative maturity of 707 PLS, a terminal
scenario can stipulate a funded local sale of some acquired pDAI producing at least 707 PLS; payment of
707 discharges the debt and releases the X pledge. That sale needs its own executable local quote and
brings pDAI back to market. An alternative is separately funded cash service while retaining the pDAI.
Without either funding source, the loan remains outstanding or enters its agreed default/liquidation
process; its accounting cannot be erased by declaring the original collateral “backed.”
No source receipt redemption or Ethereum exit is necessary for the local PLS sale or debt payment. The
collateral's exit rights still affect the lender's exposure and hence sustainable credit terms.
Local issuance: an accepted claim becomes the issuer's pool coin
Assume a compatible illustrative issuer accepts all 100 X as the required collateral for issuing 100 Y . This
is a stipulated single-collateral model, not a claim that the audited multi-asset Reserve basket accepts X
alone. Assume a separate funded market buys the 100 Y for 700 PLS. The investor spends those PLS for 
d(700) pDAI.
Participant Before After issuance, Y sale and pDAI
purchase
Source custodian 100 R allocated to X Same allocation
Investor 100 X d(700) pDAI; no unrestricted X or Y
claim retained
Issuer No collateral or Y obligations for this
position
Holds 100 X; owes the redemption
rights of 100 outstanding Y under its
stated rules
Y/PLS market At least 700 available PLS for the
modeled exchange
Holds 100 Y; its PLS falls by 700
pDAI/PLS market Its starting inventory PLS rises by 700; pDAI falls by d(700)
The market now holds Y, backed in this model by X, which represents source R. This is one claim chain,
not three independently spendable capital allocations. A later redemption retires Y against the
corresponding collateral entitlement; it cannot both retire the claim and leave the redeemer with an
independent extra Y claim. Precise basket, queue and redemption rules remain issuer-specific.
The local holder of acquired pDAI can sell it directly for PLS without redeeming Y or X. The Y market's
inventory and issuer obligations nevertheless matter to repeat issuance. More issuance can finance
more purchases only while its actual output market supplies the required local buying assets.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 291

Portal: fully backing issuance consumes the purchased pDAI
Consider a permitted DAI-reserve issuance with 100 pDAI-equivalent local aT oken claims and a
compatible wrapper. The wrapper's own deposit limits must pass at the post-mint state; token
compatibility alone does not imply deposit availability. Assume the wrapper sale pays 99.9 pDAI, actual
Portal backing fee is zero, and the actor initially contributes 0.1 pDAI. The market starts with 200 pDAI
available for the sale. Existing reserve claims and debt are held fixed; the table records changes for the
incremental cycle.
Participant/account Initial incremental position After mint, wrapper sale and full
backing
Operator 0.1 pDAI; no new receipt 0 pDAI; no receipt retained
Wrapper market 200 pDAI allocated to the modeled
trade
100.1 pDAI plus wrapper claims
representing 100 new aT oken principal
Wrapper No new aT okens or shares Holds 100 new aT oken principal;
matching wrapper shares held by the
market
Aave reserve cash No cash from this cycle +100 pDAI
Aave Portal unbacked amount 0 Rises to 100 at issuance, then returns
to 0 at full backing
Aave receipt obligations No new claims from this cycle +100 aT oken principal claims, held
through the wrapper
Conservation is explicit: the initial 200.1 pDAI becomes 100.1 market pDAI plus 100 reserve pDAI. The
operator supplies the 0.1 shortfall. No newly minted pDAI or source-chain asset is counted as reserve
cash. The underlying can be moved from the market to Aave while the market accepts a redeemable
local claim.
In general, issuance M, sale proceeds Q, and actual backing fee F require an extra max(0, M + F - Q) pDAI
for full settlement. If Q > M + F, the surplus is actual remaining cash, conditional on that premium being
obtainable. Fees credited to existing holders or protocol treasury must be added to their claim
accounting rather than treated as unowned surplus.
This is a completed funded relocation of liquidity. It does not independently establish a dollar-reference
price increase or an unlimited repeated trade. If eligible receipt holders redeem, the reserve's pDAI can
return to their hands and possibly to market. The exact local wrapper can still be useful to a financing
composition; its settlement is now explicitly financed instead of silently assumed.
The accounting follows the pinned implementation analysis in Portal accounting (Appendix 17). Whether
its caps, roles and market conditions permit the example is a separate configuration question. No
privileged action is proposed here.
Ordinary debt: two different forms of repayment
A 100-pDAI underlying repayment changes reserve cash by +100 and ordinary debt by −100. It does not
reduce Portal unbacked issuance. A payer on behalf of another borrower does not acquire that
borrower's collateral simply by paying. The borrower may become able to withdraw collateral under the
applicable rules, which can increase assets available for sale.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 292

A permitted 100-unit repayment with eligible aT okens instead reduces the borrower's debt and burns 100
units of the relevant aT oken claim. It adds no underlying reserve cash. The pinned Pool implementation
sets the aT oken-funded repayment beneficiary to the caller. This is not permissionless acquisition of
someone else's debt position through transferable debt tokens.
There is a valid conditional discount mechanism: a borrower whose eligible 100-unit debt can be
discharged with 100 eligible aT oken units may improve its balance sheet if it can acquire those claims for
90 underlying units, after costs. The difference comes from a discounted claim purchase and the pre-
existing debt obligation. It is not 10 units of newly created reserve cash, and does not prove profit for a
third party paying someone else's debt. Exact identity, transferability, conversion, debt eligibility and
costs determine applicability.
The pinned Portal/debt study (Appendix 17) governs the historical interpretation; the current Aave Pool
documentation corroborates the distinction between underlying and aT oken-funded repayment, without
replacing the pinned implementation with later protocol behavior.
Across-style delivery: source repayment changes the relayer's inventory
Use an illustrative compatible configured pair of source token T s and local token Tl. This does not
assume arbitrary source receipts can be mapped into arbitrary existing local assets. Each actual route
must satisfy its token mapping and settlement semantics. Fees are zero for this accounting example.
The participant starts with 100 T s; a relayer starts with 100 Tl locally; a separate local market has 700
PLS available to buy those 100 Tl.
Participant Before After delivery, local trades and
source repayment
Source user 100 T s No unrestricted T s; holds d(700) pDAI
locally
Source settlement custody No allocated deposit Receives 100 T s, then delivers them to
the relayer; no remaining allocation
for this settled deposit
Relayer 100 Tl locally 100 T s on source; local Tl falls by 100;
reimbursement claim is discharged
Tl/PLS market At least 700 available PLS +100 Tl, −700 PLS
pDAI/PLS market Initial inventory +700 PLS, −d(700) pDAI
The source capital remains on its source chain, now owned by the relayer. It cannot also remain an
unrestricted user asset. If T s is an admissible investment receipt, its investment may remain invested
while receipt ownership changes; that admissibility is a route condition, not a generic property of Across.
This resolves the “reverse replenishment” intuition as an inventory exchange: source capital can
reimburse a party that already provided destination capital. Neither the relayer's local inventory nor the
local market's PLS automatically replenishes. Opposite flows, additional funded relayers, purchases of
local inventory or contributed liquidity can restore them. Those are genuine ways to sustain finite further
deliveries, with costs and liabilities recorded.
The route can contain a local atomic delivery-and-trade operation where the configured application
supports it. Its later cross-chain reimbursement is not part of that same atomic transaction. The
historical architecture and current implementation limitations remain as documented in Across models
(Appendix 7) and HubPool accounting (Appendix 14).
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 293

Per-step liquidity and consolidated capacity
For actor a, asset j and ordered step n, require:
cash[a,j,n] = initial_cash[a,j] + cumulative_received[a,j,n] - cumulative_paid[a,j,n] >= 0.
Include committed credit only when it is actually drawable by that step and record the matching liability.
A terminal surplus cannot finance an earlier unfunded payment. A remote receivable due next week
does not count as today's local PLS unless an actual funder advances PLS against it.
T o combine routes, allocate explicit slices of each initial pool/treasury balance. If the same 1,000 PLS
funds both a relayer and a lender, their combined initial outlay cannot be 2,000 PLS. If earlier trades
replenish later inventory, show the actual transfers and reprice subsequent trades at their new pool
state. A receipt backing an issuer and securing a lender is one asset with an ordered claim structure, not
two independent full-value reserves.
This leaves a positive result: several genuinely independent funded routes can contribute to one
intervention budget, and restored balances can support later trades. The condition is conservation and
time order, not a restriction to one protocol or a claim that liquidity can never be reused.
Fee-inclusive local execution model
Let a constant-product pool initially contain x > 0 pDAI and y > 0 PLS. Let g = 1 - buy_fee and h = 1 -
sale_fee, with both in (0,1]. Fees stay in the pool; there is no separate removed protocol fee. A gross PLS
purchase input b >= 0 leaves:
x1 = x*y / (y + g*b) and y1 = y + b.
A subsequent holder sale of q > 0 pDAI receives:
z = y1*h*q / (x1 + h*q) PLS.
For the disclosed PLS dollar reference s > 0, the holder's local execution value is s*z/q. No Ethereum
redemption is involved. T o target T > 0, solve:
A*b² + B*b + C = 0, where
A = s*g
B = s*y*(1+g) - T*q*g
C = s*y² - T*q*y - T*x*y/h.
If the initial sale quote already meets the target, set b=0. Otherwise the required nonnegative input is:
b = (-B + sqrt(B² - 4*A*C)) / (2*A).
This follows by substituting the post-buy reserves into s*z/q=T; it accounts for the buy fee retained in the
pool rather than incorrectly keeping xy constant after a fee-paying trade. Actual fixed-point
implementations need rounding and integer-unit checks beyond these continuous equations.
With x=1,000,000, y=1,000,000,000, s=0.0001, q=1,000, T=1 and g=h=0.997, an independent 80-digit calculation
gives:
Gross initial support purchase: 2,175,295,195.262100018333 PLS.
Subsequent holder output: 10,000,000 PLS, corresponding to the stipulated $1 reference value per
pDAI over that 1,000-pDAI sale.
• 
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 294

After that sale, the next support purchase for the next identical 1,000-pDAI sale is approximately 
10,030,042.743282352925 PLS.
These are invented market inputs, not a cost estimate for real PulseChain pools. They strengthen the
previous fee-free example by exhibiting finite cost with nonzero trading fees. The explicit research batch
is Research/experiments/pulsechain_local_pls_support_20260929.json, evaluated by Research/scripts/
model_local_pls_support.py; outputs are retained under ignored artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-
support-20260929/. This derivation independently checks its formula.
Bounded sequential support and variable PLS value
A useful existence claim is: a specified finite sequence of local holder sales can receive at least
the target reference value when each is preceded by an adequately funded intervention at
the modeled state. It does not require Ethereum token redemption.
For sale event i, use current reserves (x_i,y_i), gross sale q_i and the stipulated reference s_i. Calculate
the nonnegative support purchase b_i above and then execute the mathematical state transitions:
x_plus = x_i*y_i / (y_i + g*b_i)
y_plus = y_i + b_i
z_i = y_plus*h*q_i / (x_plus + h*q_i)
x_(i+1) = x_plus + q_i
y_(i+1) = y_plus - z_i.
The support treasury pays b_i PLS and acquires x_i-x_plus pDAI. External holders deliver q_i pDAI and
receive z_i PLS. Each reserve update and each holder exit is local to PulseChain.
For treasury initial PLS R0, inflows I_i, compulsory outflows L_i, support inputs b_i and operating costs K_i,
require at every prefix n:
R0 + sum_(i<=n)(I_i - L_i - b_i - K_i) >= 0.
Treasury pDAI inventory separately equals initial inventory plus its purchased pDAI less its own sales or
commitments. Do not count external holder sales as sales of treasury inventory. A treasury sale above
target can rebuild PLS only if actual inventory and market outputs permit it; its price impact belongs in
the state recurrence.
For fixed s, the required target PLS per pDAI is fixed. For variable s_i, the target changes to T/s_i. The
same pDAI/PLS ratio no longer promises a fixed dollar-reference value. A bounded stress scenario can
specify a positive minimum PLS reference, a finite number of sales, maximum gross sale sizes, extra
costs, debt service and allowed competing flows, then compute the associated budget. An arbitrary
downward price shock or unbounded seller flow is outside that bounded claim.
The exact observed sequence model uses known q_i and s_i at each event. A stronger claim protecting
any sale up to q_max would fund the pre-event quote for q_max, recompute after each actual sale and
restrict intervening trades. A finite simulation is not proof of every possible event ordering. Support
before one sale does not guarantee the same price continuously between events, nor prevent another
trade from consuming the quote first. An execution priority or tolerated response delay belongs among
the scenario assumptions.
Thus the theory can establish a finite, fee-paying local PLS exit capacity under explicit funding and
timing. It does not need a claim that all pDAI has Ethereum backing. Its remaining economic burden is
local inventory and the obligations of the parties that supplied it, which the ledgers now identify.
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 295

Local exits versus financing-system redemptions
A pDAI holder who sells to a local pool receives its PLS; they do not have to redeem an Aave receipt,
return a source bridge token, or collect remote vault assets. Those other exit rights are still relevant to
the financing parties: a lender may seek collateral, an issuer holder may redeem Y, or a wrapper holder
may withdraw pDAI from Aave. Such flows can reduce financing availability or return additional tokens to
markets. They are stress inputs to continued support, not additional technical requirements imposed on
the pDAI holder's local exit.
This separation is the principal clarification: a local price-support and exit mechanism can be
theoretically complete without any Ethereum redemption mechanism, while still accounting
honestly for the claims and finite capital used to finance it.
Independent numerical cross-check of the six scenarios
A separate calculation recomputed every event in the six 30-event scenarios using 110-digit Decimal
arithmetic and a 420-iteration bisection search for the required purchase, rather than reusing its
quadratic solver or importing its command script. All 180 event rows matched the saved reserve, payout
and support-input values within 3.2e-70 PLS/token units. Separate cumulative pDAI and PLS conservation
checks passed at every event.
Illustrative scenario Result
Zero fee, additional 400 million PLS support reserve All 30 exits meet target; 290 million additional PLS spent
0.3% fee, additional 400 million PLS support reserve All 30 exits meet target; about 290,871,239.738011
additional PLS spent
0.3% fee, no further support reserve First below-target exit is event 2
0.3% fee, additional 100 million PLS First below-target exit is event 11
0.3% fee, reference halves at event 16, additional 400
million PLS
First below-target exit is event 16
0.3% fee, 2,000-pDAI sales, additional 400 million PLS First below-target exit is event 21
Every scenario separately funds the initial price-setting purchase. The support reserve is additional
funding, not that same initial purchase counted again. For the 1,000-pDAI sequence, the first seller uses
the already prepared quote; 29 further buys prepare the remaining 29 exits. There is no restoration after
the last modeled sale. An insufficient reserve triggers no partial support purchase under this particular
policy; a different policy would have different outputs and would need a separate calculation.
These results establish a bounded mathematical local-exit witness and show where the same witness
fails when its budget or reference assumptions change. They do not calibrate real pool reserves, seller
behavior, gas costs, debt maturities, liquidity changes, competing trades, bytecode rounding or timing.
Extension: local WPLS and forked-WETH exits, with appreciation assumed
The completed native-wrapper evidence study (Appendix 41) now confirms the exact inherited WETH at 
0xc02aaa39b223fe8d0a0e5c4f27ead9083c756cc2 withdraws native PLS. T ogether with canonical WPLS, these exact
wrappers can be normalized one-for-one into PLS units before conversion costs. The generic label/
valuation qualifications below concern unverified or different WETH-labelled assets; they do not negate
this specific native-unit finding. Contract identities and available route liquidity remain distinct.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 296

The holder's local exit can be denominated in PLS, WPLS or the specified forked-WETH contract on
PulseChain. These are alternative local output assets; none requires Ethereum redemption. WPLS can
be treated as one-for-one PLS only where its actual wrapping/redemption behavior and liquidity support
that conversion. A forked-WETH label alone does not establish either Ethereum ETH value or one-for-one
redemption into PLS. For that output, identify its exact contract, local swap inventory and its own
valuation reference.
For any chosen local output asset j, let s_j be its disclosed dollar-reference value per unit. Receiving z_j
units for q pDAI has reference execution value s_j*z_j/q. The target therefore requires T/s_j output units
per pDAI before accounting for trade-size effects and fees. PLS figures cannot be mechanically
substituted for forked-WETH amounts without the relevant exchange rate and executable market path.
If appreciation is an explicit scenario assumption, a higher s_j lowers the number of output units needed
for the same dollar-reference target. For example, a 1.5-fold increase changes T/s_j to two thirds of its
former level; a doubling halves it. A treasury holding that asset gains marked reference value, which can
improve its modeled capacity to support subsequent exits. It receives no new token units from
appreciation alone. Conversion depth, market inventory and obligations denominated in that asset still
matter.
Conversely, if the pDAI/output-asset exchange ratio remains unchanged while the output asset
appreciates, pDAI's dollar-reference price rises above its former level. A system specifically targeting one
dollar would allow or induce the pDAI/output ratio to decrease. Selling available treasury pDAI into the
market may then rebuild output-asset inventory, conditional on funded local demand and its actual price
impact. A tighter dollar target and a permanently fixed token exchange ratio are different objectives.
The direction of the mechanical effect is clear: holding the pool state, sale size and other parameters
fixed, increasing the reference raises the quoted reference value and weakly reduces the additional
support purchase needed to meet a lower-bound target. It can eliminate that immediate purchase. It
does not necessarily return the system exactly to one dollar: a lower-bound policy that buys only below
target permits above-target quotes unless a separate inventory-constrained sell policy is modeled.
The claim that attaining the pDAI target causes PLS or forked WETH to appreciate is a network-demand
hypothesis. It could be investigated through specified demand, liquidity and portfolio responses, but it is
not implied by bridge accounting or the AMM equations. A model that assumes appreciation tests its
consequences; it does not establish that causal feedback or predict the appreciation will occur. New
appreciation scenarios must remain a separate explicit experiment batch so the previous six-scenario
results stay frozen.
Independent check: selling retained pDAI after assumed appreciation
The same local model can include an inventory-constrained above-target sale. Use the saved fee_funded
state immediately after its fifteenth holder sale: approximately 316,621.864633 pDAI and
3,165,715,793.709034 PLS in the pool, 259,579,401.553066 PLS remaining support treasury, and
698,378.135367 pDAI accumulated by the operator. This model treats that pDAI as unencumbered and
available for sale. The reference shock is imposed; its occurrence is not predicted or derived from the
earlier purchases.
For an operator sale of gross a pDAI, with fee factor h, the post-sale reserves are x1=x+a and y1=x*y/(x+h*a).
Requiring the next holder's gross q sale to receive target average reference value T yields:
h*a² + [x*(1+h)+h²*q]*a + x*(x+h*q) - s*y*x*h/T = 0.
Use its nonnegative root only when the starting quote is above target and the operator owns enough
free pDAI. PLS proceeds are y*h*a/(x+h*a), transferred from pool inventory into the treasury. They are not
newly created PLS.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 297

Each row starts independently from the same fifteenth-sale checkpoint; the two results are not
cumulative or additive. Both satisfy the operator's inventory constraint, and the next holder receives $1
reference value per pDAI under that row's assumed reference. The subsequent holder sale moves the
price again; this is a checkpoint demonstration of the sell-above side of the policy, not continuous exact-
price stabilization.
An independent 450-step bisection search at 110-digit precision agrees with both quadratic roots within 
4e-104; pDAI and PLS conservation pass at retained precision. The input checkpoint itself contains 80-digit
values, so the extra arithmetic precision checks the formulas rather than adding state accuracy. The
separate analytical-checkpoint batch preserves the original six-scenario experiment and its outputs.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 298

Let R be a transferable source investment receipt and X its exclusive PulseChain representation. The

purchasing capacity concerns whether an exact accepted asset receives actual pDAI, PLS or an

Fee-inclusive local execution model
Let a constant-product pool initially contain x > 0 pDAI and y > 0 PLS. Let g = 1 - buy_fee and h = 1 -
sale_fee, with both in (0,1]. Fees stay in the pool; there is no separate removed protocol fee. A gross PLS
purchase input b >= 0 leaves:
x1 = x*y / (y + g*b) and y1 = y + b.
A subsequent holder sale of q > 0 pDAI receives:
z = y1*h*q / (x1 + h*q) PLS.
For the disclosed PLS dollar reference s > 0, the holder's local execution value is s*z/q. No Ethereum
redemption is involved. T o target T > 0, solve:
A*b² + B*b + C = 0, where
A = s*g
B = s*y*(1+g) - T*q*g
C = s*y² - T*q*y - T*x*y/h.
If the initial sale quote already meets the target, set b=0. Otherwise the required nonnegative input is:
b = (-B + sqrt(B² - 4*A*C)) / (2*A).
This follows by substituting the post-buy reserves into s*z/q=T; it accounts for the buy fee retained in the
pool rather than incorrectly keeping xy constant after a fee-paying trade. Actual fixed-point
implementations need rounding and integer-unit checks beyond these continuous equations.

Bounded sequential support and variable PLS value
A useful existence claim is: a specified finite sequence of local holder sales can receive at least
the target reference value when each is preceded by an adequately funded intervention at
the modeled state. It does not require Ethereum token redemption.
For sale event i, use current reserves (x_i,y_i), gross sale q_i and the stipulated reference s_i. Calculate
the nonnegative support purchase b_i above and then execute the mathematical state transitions:
x_plus = x_i*y_i / (y_i + g*b_i)
y_plus = y_i + b_i
z_i = y_plus*h*q_i / (x_plus + h*q_i)
x_(i+1) = x_plus + q_i
y_(i+1) = y_plus - z_i.
The support treasury pays b_i PLS and acquires x_i-x_plus pDAI. External holders deliver q_i pDAI and
receive z_i PLS. Each reserve update and each holder exit is local to PulseChain.
For treasury initial PLS R0, inflows I_i, compulsory outflows L_i, support inputs b_i and operating costs K_i,
require at every prefix n:
R0 + sum_(i<=n)(I_i - L_i - b_i - K_i) >= 0.
Treasury pDAI inventory separately equals initial inventory plus its purchased pDAI less its own sales or
commitments. Do not count external holder sales as sales of treasury inventory. A treasury sale above
target can rebuild PLS only if actual inventory and market outputs permit it; its price impact belongs in
the state recurrence.
For fixed s, the required target PLS per pDAI is fixed. For variable s_i, the target changes to T/s_i. The
same pDAI/PLS ratio no longer promises a fixed dollar-reference value. A bounded stress scenario can
specify a positive minimum PLS reference, a finite number of sales, maximum gross sale sizes, extra
costs, debt service and allowed competing flows, then compute the associated budget. An arbitrary
downward price shock or unbounded seller flow is outside that bounded claim.
The exact observed sequence model uses known q_i and s_i at each event. A stronger claim protecting
any sale up to q_max would fund the pre-event quote for q_max, recompute after each actual sale and
restrict intervening trades. A finite simulation is not proof of every possible event ordering. Support
before one sale does not guarantee the same price continuously between events, nor prevent another
trade from consuming the quote first. An execution priority or tolerated response delay belongs among
the scenario assumptions.
Thus the theory can establish a finite, fee-paying local PLS exit capacity under explicit funding and
timing. It does not need a claim that all pDAI has Ethereum backing. Its remaining economic burden is
local inventory and the obligations of the parties that supplied it, which the ledgers now identify.

Local exits versus financing-system redemptions
A pDAI holder who sells to a local pool receives its PLS; they do not have to redeem an Aave receipt,
return a source bridge token, or collect remote vault assets. Those other exit rights are still relevant to
the financing parties: a lender may seek collateral, an issuer holder may redeem Y, or a wrapper holder
may withdraw pDAI from Aave. Such flows can reduce financing availability or return additional tokens to
markets. They are stress inputs to continued support, not additional technical requirements imposed on
the pDAI holder's local exit.
This separation is the principal clarification: a local price-support and exit mechanism can be
theoretically complete without any Ethereum redemption mechanism, while still accounting
honestly for the claims and finite capital used to finance it.
